entries.title: Benjamini-Schramm bond Cayley target: universal prescribed generators
entries.statement: [DRAFT scope card; current 2026 openness UNKNOWN, with a public resolution claim awaiting review.] For every infinite finitely generated group Gamma and every finite symmetric identity-free generating set S, let G be its undirected simple Cayley graph and consider independent bond percolation. With p_c=inf{p: the root has positive probability to lie in an infinite cluster} and p_u=inf{p: exactly one infinite cluster exists almost surely}, the target asserts p_c(G)<p_u(G) iff Gamma is nonamenable. An existence theorem for a favorable generating set or a generating multiset does not establish the universal prescribed-S direction.
assumptions: Independent bond percolation; simple undirected Cayley graph

entries.title: C0047 source correction: retain degree in the spectral sufficient condition
entries.statement: [DRAFT source correction; independent frozen audit pending.] For a D-regular Cayley graph, rho denotes the l2 norm of uniform simple random walk. The published spectral sufficient condition for independent bond p_c<p_u is D*rho*p_c<1, equivalently p_c<1/(D*rho). A putative p_c<1/rho criterion drops degree; for rho<1 and p_c<=1 that malformed inequality is automatic and supplies no argument for the strict nonuniqueness phase. The condition is sufficient, not necessary. Exact source: Juschenko-Nagnibeda arXiv:1206.2183v3, Section 1, Theorem 2.

entries.title: Refuted stronger bridge: nonamenability implies D rho p_c below one
entries.statement: [REFUTED AUXILIARY ROUTE; counterexample author proof awaits audit.] The proposed statement that every nonamenable simple Cayley graph satisfies D*rho*p_c<1 is false: the standard 4-regular Cayley tree of F_2 has p_c=1/3, p_u=1 and normalized rho=sqrt(3)/2, so D*rho*p_c=2sqrt(3)/3>1. This refutes the stronger auxiliary inequality and does not refute the Benjamini-Schramm target, which holds for this tree.

entries.title: Four-regular-tree boundary for the normalized spectral route
entries.statement: [DRAFT author-proved special case; independent audit pending; no novelty claim.] For independent bond percolation on the standard Cayley tree of F_2 with generators a,a^-1,b,b^-1, p_c=1/3 and p_u=1. Uniform simple random walk has rho=sqrt(3)/2. Thus D*rho*p_c=2sqrt(3)/3>1 although p_c<p_u. A Galton-Watson exploration proves the percolation values; an end-oriented quadratic-form bound and truncated radial test functions prove the exact operator norm. The spectral sufficient condition cannot be a necessary criterion.
assumptions: Standard simple 4-regular Cayley tree of F_2

entries.title: Fixed F_2 long-power family: exact branching threshold, p_u=1, rho approaches one
entries.statement: [DRAFT author-proved special case; independent audit pending; published free-product specialization, no novelty claim.] Let G_N be Cay(F_2,{a^k:1<=|k|<=N} union {b,b^-1}), N>=1, and let chi_N(p) be the expected root-cluster size for independent bond percolation on Z with edges of lengths 1 through N. It is finite for p<1. The critical bond probability is the unique alpha_N in (0,1) satisfying alpha_N(2chi_N(alpha_N)-1)=1; there is no infinite cluster at alpha_N, and p_u(G_N)=1. Its degree is 2N+2, edge-isoperimetric infimum is exactly 2, normalized conductance is 1/(N+1), and N/(N+1)<=rho<=(N-1+sqrt(3))/(N+1)<1. Hence rho approaches one on this fixed nonamenable group while every graph has a nonempty nonuniqueness phase. For N>=2, alpha_N<0.29, established by the upper-bound quartic 4p^4-8p^3+7p^2+2p-1; its root is an upper bound, not the exact alpha_N.

entries.title: Published prior art: free-product critical equation for factor generating sets
entries.statement: [DRAFT prior-art concept.] For nontrivial finitely generated groups G_1,G_2 with finite symmetric factor generating sets, independent bond percolation on Cay(G_1*G_2,S_1 union S_2) has critical parameter characterized by (chi_1(p)-1)(chi_2(p)-1)=1, where chi_i is expected root-cluster size on the corresponding factor Cayley graph. In the F_2 long-power family, G_1=G_2=Z, the b factor has chi_b=(1+p)/(1-p), and this specializes to p(2chi_N(p)-1)=1. The union-of-factor-generators assumption is essential; this formula is not asserted for arbitrary prescribed generating sets. Source: Kozakova arXiv:math/0611668v3, Theorem 1.
assumptions: Generating set is the union of factor generating sets

relations.rationale: The bridge requires D*rho*p_c<1 for every nonamenable graph; the tree entry gives D*rho*p_c=2sqrt(3)/3>1 with p_c<p_u.
The criterion entry states sufficiency only; the tree entry shows it is not necessary.
The prior uses the union of factor generators and (chi_1-1)(chi_2-1)=1; the family sets the factors to Z and substitutes chi_b=(1+p)/(1-p).
The target quantifies over all nonamenable prescribed Cayley graphs; the family proves p_c<p_u only for its explicitly specified F_2 generating sets.
The read-only existing attempt says if p_c<1/rho for normalized walk. This correction restores the degree D in the exact cited sufficient condition.
Existing C0047 problem card states the infinite Cayley iff target with current status unverified; the draft makes its generating-set and bond quantifiers explicit without retiring it.
